summary: Linn County Fire Patrol steel tower on Scott Mountain, built 1948, manned from August 1948, removed 1979; the Bald Peter name is shared with an 1912 site.

corrections.why: The register gives 55 feet, which is 16.8 m. The brief's 16.2 m matches 53 feet, the size of the tower reported in 1947 before it was erected; the 1948 reports give 54 and 60 feet, so sources disagree and the register's figure is used.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 53 ft (1947, before erection), 54 ft (1948 patrol report), 55 ft (register) and 60 ft (1948 note). The register's 55 ft is used; the story reports the disagreement.
The register says an L-4 cab. The patrol's 1948 report describes a steel cabin, and another 1948 note says a wood cab. Not settled; the story reports both.
Removal in 1979 is agreed by all three; the words differ (removed, destroyed, dismantled). The record uses removed 1979.

The register calls the Linn tower Scott (Bald Peter), but the Bald Peter Lookout of 1912 is recorded at T12S R2E sec 28, a different place at 4,079 ft. The register's Scott Mountain (US 988) is a separate Lane County cabin. The record keeps the register's name for this tower because the patrol's 1948 description matches the register's 1948 build and 1979 removal; the name itself is flagged for a human decision.

notes_for_editor: Identity needs a human decision. The Forest Lookouts Scott Mountain page (Linn FPA, 13S-1W-31, 1948, dismantled 1979) and the register's Scott (Bald Peter) entry (Linn FPA, 1948, removed 1979, 2,136 ft) describe the same tower, so this record treats them as one. The Bald Peter name is also used for a 1912 Linn County lookout at T12S R2E sec 28 (4,079 ft), and the register's separate Scott Mountain (US 988) is a 1929 cabin in Lane County. The brief's other_names lists Scott Mountain; that name is shared with US 988, so it was not added. Height: the brief's 16.2 m is replaced by the register's 55 ft (16.8 m) as a proposed correction. Access is omitted: no source says whether the site can be visited. No source describes the site today. Not read: the Linn County Fire Patrol association's own history, or the Bald Peter 1912 site's register entry.
